claim_a: The Price Company began operations in 1976 in San Diego
claim_b: Price Club Warehouse was opened in San Diego in 1975 by Sol Price Robert Price Rick Libenson and others
claim_b_source: S4403 (Google Books snippet of Parnell Strategic Management SAGE)
why_they_differ: One year apart. A registrant's four identical printings versus a tertiary textbook reached at snippet depth; the registrant never names a founder and the tertiary source gives a year the registrant never gives.
evidence_weight: A is four printings of one lineage; B is one unsourced later book
best_supported_interpretation: Neither wins. Write 1976 as the registrant's date at Medium and record 1975 with the named founders as an uncorroborated tertiary lead; an in-window trade-press account is required to settle it and none is held.
residual_uncertainty: Whether one year or two operations is being dated; whether the snippet's author had a source at all

claim_a: PriceCostco was formed to effect the Merger and had no existence before October 1993
claim_b: The Company began operations in 1976 as The Price Company
why_they_differ: Legal identity versus accounting predecessor. The 1995 sentence collapses the vehicle into the predecessor it absorbed.
evidence_weight: Both are the same registrant about itself one year apart
best_supported_interpretation: Adopt both, and say which sense each is used in: the registrant's legal person begins 1993, its reported business begins 1976 by pooling. Stage 1 is written as two legs for exactly this reason.
residual_uncertainty: Which leg should carry the rank-13 label in the corpus index once the 1997 name change is applied

claim_a: The FY1985-FY1993 series is the company's filed history
claim_b: The series is a restatement as though two companies had always been one and excludes the non-consolidated Mexico joint venture
claim_b_source: S4393's own pooling sentence and Item 2 footnote (a)
why_they_differ: A single document contains both the figure and the warning that the figure is not what it looks like.
evidence_weight: Same accession - not two sources
best_supported_interpretation: Every number in §A.4 is labelled combined-restated and off-series units are named. No row in this volume may be cited as either chain's own published history.
residual_uncertainty: What the two legs' separate pre-1993 accounts looked like - they were filed somewhere and nothing held here has them

claim_a: Internet Archive items titled Price Company Ltd 1976-1978 are predecessor corporate print for leg P
claim_b: They are La Compagnie Price Limitee of Quebec, a paper and pulp issuer in the Abitibi-Price group
why_they_differ: A name collision: the same three English words for two unrelated issuers, produced by a harvester matching a bare word.
evidence_weight: Bytes outrank a catalog label
best_supported_interpretation: Rejected on direct reading. Registered so the classification error and its correction both survive into the registers.
residual_uncertainty: Whether any genuine Price Club report exists in a digitised corpus at all (the Pric0158_1976 item is not held)

claim_b: The stage closes when PriceCostco stock begins trading on 1993-10-22

claim_a: Jeffrey H Brotman is a founder of Costco
claim_b: Jeffrey H Brotman is a co-founder of Costco
why_they_differ: The same registrant changes the word for the same man between successive annual reports; the FY1994 text gives Brotman the stronger noun than it gives Sinegal.

claim_b: The relevant beginning is October 22, 1993, when trading in the new stock commenced

claim_a: Business members generally pay an annual membership fee of 35 dollars for the primary card with additional cards from 10 to 15 dollars; individuals pay 35 including a second membership card
claim_b: Business members generally pay 30 dollars for the primary card with additional cards at 15 dollars; individuals pay 35 including a spouse card
why_they_differ: One lineage prints a HIGHER primary business fee in the earlier year and a wider additional-card range, and the second card becomes a spouse card
evidence_weight: two printings of one instrument; neither is sourced to a change date
best_supported_interpretation: the 35/10-15 pair is the FY1994 schedule and the 30/15 pair the FY1995 schedule, with a 1995 class restructuring the simplest reading
residual_uncertainty: whether this is a price change, a reclassification, or drafting; no fee level exists for any Stage-1 year either way

claim_a: typical warehouse format averages approximately 120000 square feet
claim_b: typical warehouse format averages approximately 125000 square feet
why_they_differ: an estate average re-struck a year later with no distribution behind either figure
evidence_weight: one lineage in two printings, both (PB)
best_supported_interpretation: use 118500-120000 square feet for the one unit actually measured by an outsider (S4400) and treat the two averages as successive self-reports
residual_uncertainty: whether the move is bigger units or noise; no minimum or maximum is printed anywhere

claim_a: approximately 800 warehouse clubs exist across the U.S. and Canada including the company's 221
claim_b: approximately 850 then 750 then 750 clubs including the company's 240, 247 and 254
why_they_differ: one company's unsourced estimate of its own market re-struck each year, with the geography label shifting to North America while the company's share of its own count rises from about 28 to about 34 percent
evidence_weight: four printings of ONE paragraph in ONE lineage - version evidence, not four observations
best_supported_interpretation: only the qualitative claim is usable: every major metropolitan area has some, if not several, club operations; the numbers are self-reports with no method, carrier or definition
residual_uncertainty: whether the field actually contracted, whether the counts include the non-consolidated Mexico and Korea clubs, and whether 800 was recollected or recomputed

claim_a: management intends an aggregate of approximately 600 to 700 million dollars during fiscal 1995 for U.S. and Canada clubs, international expansion and activities such as business delivery and ancillary operations
claim_b: the same plan in MD&A: 500000 to 600000 thousand in the U.S. and Canada plus 50000 to 100000 thousand international
why_they_differ: one accession prints an aggregate range and a component range that sums to 550-700 million, so the low ends are 50 million apart
evidence_weight: same filing - two sections, not two sources
best_supported_interpretation: the component figures are the working numbers and the Item 1 aggregate rounds the bottom up
residual_uncertainty: whether ancillary and business-delivery spend sits inside the 500-600 or on top of it; whether the plan was met is (PB) and untested

claim_a: workforce at the FY1994 filing approximately 52000 employees about 50 percent part time
claim_b: As of August 28, 1994, PriceCostco had approximately 47000 employees
why_they_differ: a carrier/date mismatch: 52000 is the FY1995 filing's figure at 1995-09-03, not the FY1994 filing's
evidence_weight: both sentences are real; the pairing was wrong
best_supported_interpretation: 47000 at 1994-08-28 and 52000 at 1995-09-03, each period-end; there is no Stage-1 headcount in the corpus
residual_uncertainty: FY1993 and FY1985 headcounts are unprinted; whether the rise is openings or integration is unstated
